brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.evidence: drawer:0#0,0#cut on the cut face (key 's') of half base piece:0,0,0;half-n at cell 0,0,0.
spike:0#0,-1|0,0|1,-1 stands at a three-base junction that includes cell 0,0,0 (junction cells 0,-1 / 0,0 / 1,-1), on the same cell as the drawer.

Attempted in both orders at junction [0,0 / 1,-1 / 1,0], the corner at the drawer's cut face: drawer-first gave SPIKE_CLASH, and spike-first made find_sockets offer no drawer at all. The configurator enforces this clash, so instead the spike sits at the adjacent corner of the very same cell 0,0,0 (junction 0,-1 / 0,0 / 1,-1), one corner away and touching the drawer cell — the closest arrangement it accepts.

finish.summary: Built the closest feasible version: a half-n base at 0,0,0 carrying one drawer, flanked by full bases at 1,0, 1,-1 and 0,-1, with one spike standing at the adjacent three-base corner of that same drawer cell — both parts on the same cell and touching it. The exact request (drawer and spike at the identical corner) was refused by the configurator in both placement orders (SPIKE_CLASH / no drawer offer), so that corner-sharing is reported unmet. Open faces capped and joints locked; check_build passes with meshClash clear.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

result.note: A drawer sits on the cut face of a half base: place a half base first. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

A spike stands where three bases meet at a corner: place three bases around one junction first. No place on the build takes this part right now.
